criteria.note: The negative half of NVA-A29-6 (no-child/wrong-child/wrong-attempt/wrong-fingerprint/replay/host-only/CAS-health/fallback all fail to reach available-attested) is fully demonstrated by the reducer's own contract tests above. The positive half -- a fresh, real opt-in selected-child execution producing a genuine childReceipt -- is UNREACHABLE from this session: a repository-wide search (grep for reduceSelectedSandboxDisposition/createSelectedSandboxDisposition across plugins/pipeline-core) found the reducer consumed only by its own test file and by plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/invocation-preflight.mjs, which only calls validateSelectedSandboxDisposition on an already-existing disposition record -- it does not spawn a child process or emit a probe-start/probe-success event pair anywhere. There is currently no wired production launcher in this repository that would attempt a real selected-sandbox child execution through this contract; writing one is new production code, which is out of scope for this evidence-sealing task (briefing NOVA-A29-EVIDENCE-1 field 4). This is a stronger and more specific finding than a session sandbox permission denial: git and codex CLI (codex-cli 0.147.0) both execute successfully in this session (`git --version` and `codex --version` verified via spawnSync/exec, exit 0, no EPERM), so the blocker is the absence of integration wiring, not (in this session) a host permission denial. The matrix's prior 'workspace EPERM' framing describes an different, already-superseded observation (result.md, the critic-packet-preflight git-temp-repo fixture); it does not apply to this contract, which has no live-launch call site to even attempt.
